install_recipe:
apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential curl
git config --global --add safe.directory /work/<repo>   # required, else every git command dies with 'dubious ownership'
curl -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs -o /tmp/rustup.sh && sh /tmp/rustup.sh -y --default-toolchain stable
# 'stable' currently resolves to 1.98.1; pin with 'rustup toolchain install 1.98.1 && rustup default 1.98.1' for byte-identical builds
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
cd <repo>   # checked out at the parent commit; Cargo.lock from that commit pins every crate
cargo test --no-run -p clap   # first run downloads all dependencies from crates.io (network egress required once)
issue_paraphrase: An argument that is marked hidden for help output can still change the layout of the plain --help text: if the hidden argument carries a list of possible values and any of those values has a description (which the derive-based API fills in automatically from documentation), --help switches from the compact one-line option listing to the long help layout. The hidden argument's option suddenly wraps its help onto two lines and appends a '(see a summary with '-h')' hint, even though the whole point of hiding is that the argument should not influence help at all.
fix_summary: The should_long predicate that decides whether an argument forces the long help layout now first checks !arg.is_hide_set() — a completely hidden argument can no longer trigger long help regardless of possible-value help texts. For the author only; must not leak into instruction.md.
notes: Tested in bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 (root) + rustc/cargo 1.98.1. Build: 'cargo test --no-run -p clap' compiles the clap lib and the trybuild test binaries; once the crates.io cache is warm this takes ~13 s with 64 cores (the clap lib itself ~6 s), the equivalents at 1 CPU are roughly 2-5 minutes cold; the actual test binary run is 0.00-0.2 s. Run ONLY the single test via '<globbing target/debug/deps/builder-* binary> --test <fn name>'; the test binary name includes a content hash so use ls -t target/debug/deps/builder-* . Do not gate on plain 'cargo test' (it executes every test binary incl. examples/ui/macros); the builder suite is what matters and passes fully at the fix (811/811). No network needed at test time. Non-ASCII/terminal width/env vars are not needed. Note the parent commit is a merge commit ('Merge pull request #4711'); its tree builds fine.

issue_paraphrase: A CLI defined through the builder API can attach a default value to one argument that is conditional on another argument's presence, listing several such conditions at once through the OS-string flavor of the API. When the condition is named by a plain argument id string, the conditional defaults silently never trigger: parsing succeeds, the triggering flag keeps its value, but the dependent argument reports having no value at all, as if the condition had never been registered. The same conditions supplied through the non-OS API work, which makes the failure appear data-dependent and hard to diagnose.
fix_summary: Arg::default_value_ifs_os now forwards each conditional key directly (arg instead of arg.key()) to default_value_if_os, avoiding hashing the argument id twice, so the stored conditional id matches the parsed argument's id and the default applies. For the author only; must not leak into instruction.md.
notes: Tested in bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 (root) + rustc/cargo 1.98.1. This parent/fix pair is from the pre-4.0 development line (Cargo.toml reports version 3.1.18 / MSRV 1.56) but the tree is self-contained and builds cleanly with modern stable rustc; the test framework (trybuild) is identical to the 4.1-era entries, so run mechanics are the same: build with 'cargo test --no-run -p clap', execute with the target/debug/deps/builder-* binary plus '--test default_value_ifs_os'. 1577 builder tests all pass at the fix. The test contains non-ASCII bytes (标记2) - the test harness handles them; keep the file byte-identical when extracting it with 'git show <fix>:tests/builder/arg_settings.rs'. No runtime network; compile is the whole cost (~13 s at 64 cores warm, minutes at 1 CPU cold).
